description: 15 real production scenarios. Each maps to a Cedar policy in policies.yaml.

scenarios.name: Large wire transfer blocked — dual approval required
scenarios.narrative: AI agent processing overnight settlements attempts to wire $75,000 to a correspondent bank. Amount exceeds $50k threshold. AGR routes to compliance officer for approval before funds move.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Without AGR, this $75,000 wire executes automatically at 2am. With AGR, your compliance team gets an email and must approve before a single dollar moves.

scenarios.name: OFAC-sanctioned country wire blocked immediately
scenarios.narrative: Agent processes a payment request. Destination country Iran (IR) is on the OFAC sanctions list. AGR denies immediately — no approval path exists.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Automated payments to sanctioned countries are a federal crime. AGR blocks this in under 50ms with a full audit trail, before any bank API is called.

scenarios.name: After-hours large ACH batch requires approval
scenarios.narrative: Payroll agent submits a $250,000 ACH batch at 11pm. After-hours large batches require manual review to prevent fraud.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: ACH fraud peaks after hours. AGR catches this automatically — the batch sits in queue until a human approves it on the dashboard.

scenarios.name: Routine payroll batch allowed automatically
scenarios.narrative: Weekly payroll agent submits $380,000 payroll batch. Classified as payroll, under $500k limit — allowed instantly.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: AGR does not slow down legitimate operations. Low-risk, pre-classified actions flow through in under 10ms.

scenarios.name: Payment to unverified vendor blocked
scenarios.narrative: Accounts payable agent tries to pay a new vendor whose KYC has not been completed. AGR blocks the payment until vendor verification is done.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Business email compromise (BEC) fraud often targets new vendor setups. AGR enforces KYC completion before any payment goes out.

scenarios.name: Equity trade blocked — exceeds 5% position limit
scenarios.narrative: Trading agent attempts to buy 6.2% of outstanding shares in a small-cap stock. FINRA position limit violated. Blocked before order hits the exchange.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: FINRA position limits exist to prevent market manipulation. AGR enforces them in real time — the agent never reaches the exchange API.

scenarios.name: Block trade above $1M requires compliance approval
scenarios.narrative: Agent executes algorithmic block trade worth $1.8M. MiFID II requires pre-trade transparency for orders of this size.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: MiFID II block trade rules are complex. AGR enforces them as a simple policy — any agent hitting this threshold pauses for review.

scenarios.name: Options trade blocked — account not margin-enabled
scenarios.narrative: Agent attempts to write covered calls on a cash account. Options require margin account. Blocked to prevent regulatory breach.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Executing options on an ineligible account triggers FINRA violations. AGR prevents this at the policy layer — not after the trade settles.

scenarios.name: FX trade blocked outside market hours for non-24h pair
scenarios.narrative: Agent tries to execute EURUSD trade at 1am EST. Non-24h FX pairs have restricted trading windows.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Off-market FX execution has large spread costs and settlement risk. AGR enforces trading hours as policy — no spreadsheet needed.

scenarios.name: Short sell blocked on circuit-breaker stock
scenarios.narrative: Agent tries to short-sell a stock that has triggered the SEC circuit breaker (Alternative Uptick Rule). Blocked immediately.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: The SEC Alternative Uptick Rule is triggered dynamically. AGR ingests the flag as context — the agent cannot short even if the code tells it to.

scenarios.name: SAR filing requires senior compliance approval
scenarios.narrative: AML monitoring agent identifies suspicious pattern and attempts to auto-file a Suspicious Activity Report. Filing requires human review.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Wrongly filed SARs expose the bank to legal liability. Correct ones are legally required. AGR ensures a human signs off on every filing.

scenarios.name: Audit record deletion blocked within retention window
scenarios.narrative: Agent attempts to purge old transaction logs. Records are 4 years old — SOX requires 7-year retention. Blocked.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: SOX Section 802 makes destroying financial records a federal crime. AGR enforces 7-year retention as a policy — not as a developer's memory.

scenarios.name: Compliance officer read access allowed
scenarios.narrative: Compliance AI agent reads customer financial history for quarterly review. Role is compliance_officer — permitted.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: AGR enables agents to do their job. Legitimate access flows through instantly — governance does not mean blanket blocking.

scenarios.name: Bulk PII export blocked — DPO approval required
scenarios.narrative: Data science agent attempts to export 15,000 customer records including PII for model training. GDPR Art.25 requires Data Protection Officer sign-off.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: GDPR fines are 4% of global revenue. This one policy prevents the most common GDPR violation — bulk PII export without DPO review.

scenarios.name: Model training on live transactions blocked
scenarios.narrative: ML agent tries to train a fraud model directly on live transaction data without anonymization. Blocked — violates data minimization principle.
scenarios.leadership_talking_point: Training AI on live PII without anonymization violates GDPR Art.5. AGR blocks the training job before a single record is read.
